output.methodChoice: D+C: compare rival hypotheses against per-cell timing and check the cause on the natural experiment, since the leadership story and the timing conflict.
output.brief: Don't roll back gateway 5.8. The regression comes from the 2 Nov storage compaction tuning change (FC-7710), not from the gateway. The change raised compaction threads from 2 to 6. Disk use went from 41% to 97% within 5 minutes of the push, and disk read queue wait rose from 9 ms to 205 ms. In every cell, latency rose within minutes of the push, regardless of when 5.8 arrived. For example, use-1 got 5.8 at 22:05 but didn't degrade until after the push. aps-3 skipped the push, got 5.8, and stayed at about 94 ms. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 on 6 Nov changed nothing. Network and traffic growth don't fit the timing. A rollback would take about 4 hours and would reopen the signature vulnerability. The audit deadline is 30 Nov. Next step: revert the compaction change in one cell, for example use-1, and watch p99 and backlog. Then extend the revert to the other cells if it works. Backlog was 11.2% on 2 Nov, below the 15% level where problems start, so watch it. Don't pause compaction. Rate-limiting Orrin is premature, because the backlog attribution job reports on 10 Nov. Confidence is high on the cause. It is moderate on what drove the backlog growth.
